_: HIGH-WATER MARKS for test coverage. Raised by --update, NEVER lowered by code. The money path is tracked separately because a repo-wide average lets order-path coverage fall while research tests keep the aggregate up -- the average hides exactly the number worth watching.
next_ceiling: STILL money-path parity, and the gap is still the point. 41.6% -> 70.45% (2026-08-06) against 92.46% repo-wide: the direction is right and the inversion is not fixed. ~221 uncovered statements remain on the code that can place orders and move funds, and the three defects found writing those tests -- a flatten leg that could sell through zero, and GAP #49 wired into only one leg of a two-leg trade -- were all in the untested part, which is the whole argument. Parity is not the end either: the ceiling after it is the FAILURE branches specifically, since every incident this desk has had came from an error path, not a happy one. Per L1.50 the floor is the minimum and 100% is the target; the residue above is named so it cannot be mistaken for work already done.
_merge_note: 2026-08-09 three-way merge (Claude branch + Codex unified frontier). Floors resolved as the MAX OF EACH FIELD INDEPENDENTLY, never by taking a side: repo 93.23 (claude) vs 93.24 (codex) -> 93.24; money path 81.55 (claude) vs 89.44 (codex) -> 89.44. L1.50 says floors ratchet UP only, and a merge is not a measurement -- picking one side wholesale would have silently lowered whichever floor that side happened to be behind on. `measured` is taken from the codex side because that is the branch whose suite last produced it; the next real run overwrites it.

retired_floors.earned_over: the repo INCLUDING the Binance/crypto execution stack
retired_floors.why_retired: The crypto execution stack was deleted under the MT5-only mandate: 5 libs/execution connectors, ~14 crypto scripts and ~50 test files, in commits dc58cd73/dadac868. That code was WELL covered, so removing it and its tests lowered the repo-wide average without making any surviving line less tested. 93.24% described a population that no longer exists; 86.48% is the honest coverage of what remains. This is a POPULATION CHANGE, not a regression -- the same reasoning the money-path floor already applies automatically when its file set changes, applied by hand here because the repo floor has no automatic migration path and --update only ever RAISES.

repo_floor_rebase_why: rebased 93.24 -> 86.48 after the crypto stack was deleted; the retired floor is preserved in `retired_floors` with the population that earned it. NOTHING about the surviving code got worse, and the ratchet resumes from the new baseline: it may only rise from here.
